git-vc.def: Software that records every saved version of a project's files, with who changed what and why, so you can compare and go back.

git-git.def: The version-control program on your computer; it keeps a folder's history in a hidden .git folder and works offline.

git-github.def: A website that hosts copies of Git repositories online for backup, sharing, collaboration and your portfolio.

git-repo.def: A folder whose history Git keeps. Created with git init or copied with git clone.

git-ignore.def: A file listing names and patterns (like .venv/, *.csv) that Git should never track.

git-pat.def: A password-like string generated on GitHub and used instead of your password when Git talks to GitHub over HTTPS.

git-remote.def: A named link to a copy of the repository elsewhere, usually GitHub; origin is the conventional name.

git-clone.def: Copies a whole repository, with all its history, into a new folder.

git-branch.def: A separate line of commits for trying an idea; main is the default. Combine with git merge.

git-commit.def: A save point: a snapshot of the staged changes with a message, an author and an ID (a hash).

git-staging.def: Where git add puts changes chosen for the next commit.
